pieces.title: Three teachers, three tools
pieces.caption: The page ties two of its three disciplines to a teacher. The dichotomy of control grows from the fortress Epictetus discovered, and the view from above is what Marcus practices. It names no one teacher for the four virtues. *What is real and what is a choice:* The two pairings join sentences from different sections of the page; no one sentence there says Epictetus gave the dichotomy. Every gloss is the page's own wording. The two red ties are 'contradicts' links in the map build of 2026-11-09, declared on Seneca's and Epictetus's pages and absent from this page's text. The left-to-right order is the maker's; the page lists slave, statesman, emperor. *Leaking in:* Seneca and Epictetus: each page's links hold one of the two contradictions drawn in red ('wealthy-statesman-vs-dispossessed-slave' on Seneca, 'slave-pole-vs-throne' on Epictetus).

challenge.by: challenger · light round, batch E (sheets from heroes, avatars and records) · read-only dispatch

verdicts.file: Stoicism — rich — three teachers, three tools.png
verdicts.why: The top row is the page's sentence and is right, but the three grey rules that drop from each teacher to a "move" pair them wrongly: Seneca over The Dichotomy of Control, Epictetus over The View From Above, Marcus over The Four Virtues. The page gives the dichotomy to Epictetus (prohairesis is "the seed of" it) and the view from above to Marcus ("Marcus practices looking down").

remade.file: Stoicism — rich — three teachers, three tools.png
remade.what: The grey rules paired each teacher with the wrong discipline, one of two contradictions was left out, and the caption stated no claim. The disciplines now sit under the teacher the page ties them to with only those two ties drawn, both contradictions are drawn, and every gloss is the page's wording.
